feature1.prompt: In the Django admin, inlines for auto-created ManyToManyFields are editable even when the user has only the view permission. This feature focuses on refactoring the permission checking logic to make it more maintainable and consistent. The goal is to introduce a unified helper method that consolidates permission validation for adding, changing, deleting, and viewing inline objects. After the refactoring, the overall behavior should remain the same, but the underlying implementation will be cleaner and easier to extend in the future.
feature1.hint_texts: Introduce the _has_any_perms_for_target_model helper method in django/contrib/admin/options.py to centralize the permission checks. Update the has_add_permission, has_change_permission, has_delete_permission, and has_view_permission methods to delegate to this new helper. The focus here is on improving code clarity and reducing redundancy without modifying the user-facing behavior. Make sure that the refactored code continues to honor the existing permission semantics.
feature1.entrypoint: File: django/contrib/admin/options.py. Add the new method _has_any_perms_for_target_model and refactor the following methods: has_add_permission, has_change_permission, has_delete_permission, and has_view_permission. Start changes around the existing permission-related code (near line 2111) where these methods are defined.

feature2.prompt: In the Django admin, inlines for auto-created ManyToManyFields are editable even when the user has only the view permission. This feature targets the bug where users with view-only permissions can add, change, or delete inline records. The fix should enforce that only users with the proper change permission are allowed to modify these ManyToManyField inlines. After the fix, a user with only view permission will see the inline content in a read-only mode without options to edit or remove the records.
feature2.hint_texts: Revise the permission logic in the affected methods to ensure that editing actions (add, change, delete) are allowed only when the user has the 'change' permission. Specifically, modify has_add_permission, has_change_permission, and has_delete_permission to use the helper method with the appropriate permission list. Adjust has_view_permission to require either the view or change permission as a fallback, thereby enforcing a stricter access control. The focus here is on correcting the unintended editability of the inlines for users with view-only rights.
feature2.entrypoint: File: django/contrib/admin/options.py. Update the permission checking conditions within has_add_permission, has_change_permission, has_delete_permission, and has_view_permission so that they enforce the 'change' permission correctly on auto-created ManyToManyField inlines. Concentrate on the logic that distinguishes between view-only access and permitted modifications.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: The primary shared resource is the file django/contrib/admin/options.py, particularly the ModelAdmin permission methods and the newly introduced _has_any_perms_for_target_model helper method. Both features also interact with the admin inline components and the associated test modules in tests/admin_inlines.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Feature1 provides the refactored API for permission checking that Feature2 relies on to enforce correct permission behavior. Both features must be merged together so that the refactoring does not conflict with the bug fix. Coordination in testing and code review stages is essential to ensure that the unified helper method is used consistently and that the overall permission enforcement works as expected.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers responsible for Feature1 and Feature2 need to coordinate closely on method signatures and the integration of the helper method. Discussions should focus on how the refactoring impacts the permission checks and the adjustments required in the bug fix. Regular updates and joint integration testing will help to ensure that changes made in one feature do not adversely affect the other.
